newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian markets edgy ahead of election campaign.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian markets edgy ahead of election campaign.

text.p: Indonesian financial markets were edgy on Friday, with the rupiah briefly hitting another historic low against the dollar, amid worries about possible unrest during the upcoming election campaign.
Nervousness on the stock market was kept in check, but profit-taking pushed the composite index down 0.27 percent to 651.25 points by the midsession, brokers and dealers said.
The campaign officially begins on Sunday. The general election itself is on May 29.
The rupiah, which fell 15 points on Thursday, plunged again on Friday morning to 2,440.50 to the dollar from 2,432.50 at the open on fears of campaign violence, dealers said.
By midday, it had recovered to 2,437.00/38.00.
Dealers said the speed of the fall was less dramatic than on Thursday because investors were confident about the economy's fundamentals.
They said the rupiah decline was exacerbated by options-related and stop-loss selling.
"It's a reflection of the concern that people have going in to the election. It's pretty much within expectations," Winston Koh, a vice-president at JP Morgan in Singapore, told Reuters.

"What is interesting is that the action is pretty much in the spot market. In the forward market, the forward points were little changed," Koh said, adding that forward points reflected underlying concerns about fundamentals.
"In a sense, it's comforting," he said.
Pardy Kendy, treasury head of PT Bank Buana Indonesia, said he expected the rupiah's volatility to ease next week if the launch of the campaign passes peacefully.
"Operators usually prepare for everything possible ahead of a certain event. If there is nothing major, I think the market is going to settle down," Kendy said.
"They are just trying to factor in possible disturbances."
Economists also remained confident the rupiah would recover after the election.
"Post-election we should see the rupiah trading stronger relative to the (central bank's intervention) band. It would possibly trade towards the bottom (of the band) once again," Koh said.
The band allows the central bank to intervene in the foreign exchange market if rates fall out of the range. It was fixed at 2,404/2,596 on Thursday.
Koh said the long-term rupiah view remained bullish because most people were expecting the currency to depreciate less than the usual four to five percent this year.
"There is still a lot of interest in long rupiah. It's a question when to get into the market," Koh said.
"Most people are still very comfortable with the long-term view, just as in the short-term they expect that there will be more volatility," he added.
On the stock market, brokers said the nervousness was limited. But there was some profit-taking in market heavyweights which could be attributed to the fears over the upcoming campaign, they said.
Among large-capitalisation stocks to fall prey to profit-taking were telecommunications giant Telkom and tobacco companies HM Sampoerna and Gudang Garam.
